clue.text: Ex-con bedding bird in hay wagon's no Romeo. He wasn't always like this

indicators.note: Romeo is the radio code for R, and 'no' tells us to drop that letter
to bed something is to take it into your bed, so the outer word holds the rest
one piece sits inside the next one along

blocks.note: an old lag is a former prisoner
a wain is a farm wagon, as in Constable's The Hay Wain
the word bird without its R

explanation.surface: A reformed convict who once slept with a girl in a haycart is now no romantic hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' looks like a girlfriend, or prison time served, but it is only a word to trim. An old lag is British slang for a habitual convict.
explanation.definitionFit: The cryptic definition describes a reformed criminal: an ex-con who now obeys the rules was not always so honest.

clue.text: Adapt article by bishop in Time

indicators.note: the first pieces are placed inside the word for time

blocks.note: Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
the indefinite article
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A churchman is asked to rework a magazine piece for Time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' looks like the news magazine, but it is just a period of time. Right Reverend is the formal style of an Anglican bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange music is to adapt it for different instruments or voices.

clue.text: Permitted broadcast for all to hear

indicators.note: something broadcast reaches us through our ears, so we go by sound

blocks.note: permitted means let, or allowed

explanation.surface: Something approved for transmission so that everyone may listen.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something out loud means speaking audibly, so everyone present can hear it.

clue.text: Hotel shortly free to entertain the king for profit

indicators.note: cut short, so the word loses its final letter
to entertain guests is to take them in, so these letters hold another piece

blocks.note: an inn is a hotel; cut short it loses one N
to ease is to free or relieve
Carolus Rex, the Latin abbreviation for King Charles

explanation.surface: A small hotel is happy to host the monarch without charge in the hope of making money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hotel' is the inn, not the radio code H. Carolus Rex is Latin for King Charles, so CR is a crossword king.
explanation.definitionFit: An increase is a gain or growth, and a profit is a gain in money.

clue.text: Unlikelihood of embassies pulling out of grand manoeuvring

indicators.note: taking something out of a group removes it, here one letter
manoeuvring moves things around into new positions

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, minus a G
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Diplomatic missions withdrawing from some great political manoeuvre seems an improbable event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulling out' looks like the embassies withdrawing, but the words are 'out of grand', removing G from the fodder before it is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Implausibility is the quality of not being believable, which is the same as unlikelihood.

clue.text: Hurried clear of society after joker turned up and stared

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top
being clear of something means it has been removed

blocks.note: a wag is a joker
sped means hurried
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: Someone rushed away from a party after a prankster arrived and then gaped.
explanation.walkthrough: The word order puts 'after' between the pieces: the reversed joker comes first, with SPED minus S behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: To gawp is a British informal word for staring openly and foolishly, so gawped means stared.

clue.text: Foundation graduates given low grade

blocks.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts
E is a low mark in exams

explanation.surface: A college's founding graduates were handed poor marks.
explanation.definitionFit: A base is what something rests on, its foundation or support.

clue.text: Strangers meeting bandit led astray

indicators.note: led astray means lead off the right path, so the letters wander out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Unfamiliar people encounter an outlaw who has been misled.
explanation.definitionFit: A blind date is a romantic meeting arranged between two people who have never met.

clue.text: Cover girl suppresses ardent desire

indicators.note: to suppress something is to hold it down within, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: she refers to a girl
heat is passion or ardent desire

explanation.surface: A cover-girl model hides her intense feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover girl' looks like one phrase, but 'Cover' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe a blade is to put it in its scabbard, so the word means to cover or encase.

clue.text: So very dismissive of outsiders being given work

indicators.note: dismissing the outer letters leaves only the ones in the middle

blocks.note: the inner letters of very
to go is to work or function

explanation.surface: Someone extremely contemptuous of strangers gets a job anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, used in English to mean so or consequently.

clue.text: Ad agency employee's instruction to plagiarise?

blocks.note: first meaning: a person who writes the text of adverts
second meaning, read as two words: an order to reproduce an author's work

explanation.walkthrough: Split in two, the answer is an imperative telling someone to lift a writer's words, which is plagiarism.
explanation.definitionFit: In advertising the person who composes slogans and text is known by this job title.

clue.text: Tense United ultimately finished game exhausted

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end, so only the final letter is used
an exhausted word has been emptied out, leaving only its outside

blocks.note: united as one
the final letter of finished
the outside letters of game

explanation.surface: Nervous Manchester United fans watched their side finally finish the match worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a football club, but it is just ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge is an idiom for being nervous and jumpy, the same as tense.

clue.text: Yarn took in most of new Conservative party bores

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter
a drill bores into something, so these letters go inside another word

blocks.note: new without its final letter
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a do is a party
ate means took in food

explanation.surface: A tall tale fooled most people, and new Tory party members are tiresome.
explanation.walkthrough: NE + C + DO bores into ATE. 'Bores' looks like dull people; it is the verb, to drill into.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarn is an informal word for a story, and an anecdote is a short entertaining story.

clue.text: Member of the Lords half-heartedly takes seat, having succeeded, and carries on

indicators.note: losing half its heart means one of the two middle letters is dropped
having something means holding it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a peer sits in the House of Lords; one E removed from its centre
sits means takes a seat
S is the abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: A reluctant new peer sits down in the Lords after inheriting the title and keeps going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeded' suggests inheriting a title; in crosswords it is just the abbreviation S, which goes in the middle of the seat-taking word.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist is to continue steadily in spite of difficulty, which is carrying on.

clue.text: Criminal using very detailed measurement

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so these letters are twisted

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crook relies on extremely precise sizing-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Surveying is the careful measuring of land to map its boundaries and heights.

clue.text: Barbies regularly date between the sheets

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is used

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: A doll gets a regular romantic engagement with Ken, in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Abed is an old word for in bed, which is what between the sheets means.

clue.text: Sweet? Well, it's a pharmacy counter that stocks it

indicators.note: a shop that stocks an item holds it inside, so the letters lie within these words
counter means running in the opposite direction, so read backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters hidden inside these words, starting just after the W

explanation.surface: Asked whether something is a sweet, the answer is that it is sold over a chemist's counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pharmacy counter' looks like the shop counter; 'counter' is the reversal signal. The letters run backwards from the P of pharmacy to the E of well.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastille is a small sweet or a medicated lozenge, often fruit-flavoured.

clue.text: Endlessly bitter plant

indicators.note: with no end, so the last letter is removed

blocks.note: acerb is a rare word for sour or bitter, minus its final letter

explanation.surface: A perpetually sour houseplant.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is the botanical genus of maples, so an acer is a type of tree, a plant.

clue.text: Schoolteacher is happily embracing nurse

indicators.note: embracing means holding within, so the letters lie inside these words

blocks.note: the run of letters from the end of the first word to the start of the third

explanation.surface: A teacher is glad to hug a hospital worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurse' looks like a medical worker; here it is a verb, to nurture.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a hope or a grudge is to hold it fondly in mind, as to cherish it.

clue.text: Church rent met by 60% of brass band?

indicators.note: sixty per cent of a five-letter word keeps three letters and drops two

blocks.note: the first three of its five letters
Church of England
to let is to rent out

explanation.surface: A church's hire fee is paid by part of a brass band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass band' looks like a musical group; the question mark flags band as a ring worn on the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is a decorative band worn around the wrist, which the question mark hints at.

clue.text: Proscribe distribution of bergamot to a large extent

indicators.note: only to a large extent means most but not all, so the last letter goes
distribution spreads things around, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: bergamot without its final letter

explanation.surface: Ban the widespread sale of a citrus oil used in Earl Grey.
explanation.definitionFit: To embargo trade or goods is to officially forbid them, which is what proscribe means.

clue.text: Problem with Chinese dog rearing up

indicators.note: in a down clue, rearing up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the Han are China's majority people
a pug is a small breed of dog

explanation.surface: Trouble with a Chinese dog standing on its hind legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinese dog' reads as one breed, like a Pekingese, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A hang-up is an informal word for a neurosis or problem that bothers someone.

clue.text: Treacherous couples leading revolutionary networks gamble with death

indicators.note: a couple is a pair, and the leading pair of letters from each word is kept

blocks.note: first two letters
first two letters
first two letters
first two letters

explanation.surface: Treacherous insurgent cells take risks with their lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couples' looks like pairs of people; it is pairs of letters taken from the front of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade deserts a cause, so as an adjective it means traitorous.

clue.text: Beats produced by legendary hammer-wielder moving right behind stage initially

indicators.note: moving one letter to a new place changes the order of the name
initially means at the start, so only first letters are used

blocks.note: Thor is the Norse god with the hammer Mjolnir
first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Drumbeats come from a mythical god swinging his hammer backstage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' is R, which moves one place earlier in the god's name. 'Behind stage' looks like backstage, but gives two initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a strong regular pulse or beat, like a heartbeat.

clue.text: Puzzle about capsized vessel

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, so in a down clue the word is turned over

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
a sub is a submarine, a vessel

explanation.surface: A mystery surrounds an overturned ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a puzzle in which pictures and symbols stand for words or syllables.

clue.text: Nautical chamber composition of Gilbert and Sullivan denied a last run, unfortunately

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters are arranged anew
being denied something means going without it, so letters are taken away
something gone wrong is in disorder, so the letters to be removed appear in any order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A Gilbert and Sullivan opera, sadly refused a final run of performances.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a subtractive anagram: strike out the letters of 'a last run' in any order from the composers' names and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A diving bell is an open-bottomed chamber lowered into the sea to hold divers underwater.

clue.text: Beethoven's first bit of work as a Viennese composer

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter only

blocks.note: the opening letter
an erg is a small unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: The start of a Beethoven piece is treated as the work of another Viennese composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of work' looks like a musical piece, but an erg is the physics unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was a twentieth-century composer born in Vienna, a pupil of Schoenberg.

clue.text: Diver finally inspects North Sea rig

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of each of the following words

blocks.note: the last letter of each word

explanation.surface: An underwater worker at last checks an offshore oil platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diver' looks like a person in a wetsuit, but it is a seabird, the shag, a kind of cormorant that dives for fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The shag is a seabird related to the cormorant that dives underwater to catch fish.

clue.text: Post Office meeting about closure of surplus property

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes around a letter
the closure of a word is where it ends, so the last letter is kept

blocks.note: PO is the abbreviation for Post Office
a session is a meeting
the final letter

explanation.surface: A post office meeting discusses shutting down extra property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closure' suggests shutting a branch, as many British post offices have been; here it just means the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A possession is something you own, an item of property.
